## Verdict

Prior empty/`None` guard on `total()` is fixed; `first_name()` empty-name crash remains open.

## Prior findings

1. **`5d977ce4424f3a31` (resolved)** — `total()` now returns `0` when `items` is falsy (`None` or `[]`), so callers that pass `None` no longer hit `TypeError` on `sum(...)`.
2. **`09584834c0aebae2` (open)** — `first_name()` is still `user.name.split()[0]` with no empty-name guard; `"".split()[0]` raises `IndexError`.

## Notes

Small, focused follow-up. No new issues on the `total()` guard itself.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

5d977ce4424f3a31: if not items: return 0 handles both None and empty list before sum().
09584834c0aebae2: first_name still does user.name.split()[0] with no empty-string guard.

prior_findings_kept.body: first_name() crashes on an empty name ('' .split()[0] → IndexError). first_name still does user.name.split()[0] with no empty-string guard.
